  • Narcissistic PD: grandiosity, lack of empathy, need for admiration
  • Most frequently EPPP-tested cluster

  • Avoidant PD: social inhibition, feelings of inadequacy, hypersensitivity to rejection
  • Dependent PD: excessive need to be cared for, submissiveness, fear of separation
  • OCPD: ego-syntonic perfectionism, orderliness, rigidity
  • OCPD most prevalent PD in general population (3–8%)
  • All traits ego-syntonic; anxiety internalized

title: SEM vs. SEE vs. Sdiff: Key Distinctions
html:
SEM vs. SEE vs. Sdiff: Key Distinctions
SEM
  • Standard Error of Measurement
  • Formula: SD * sqrt(1 - r_xx)
  • Uses reliability coefficient
  • Precision of a single observed score
  • Builds confidence intervals: 68% CI = score +/- 1 SEM; 95% CI = score +/- 1.96 SEM
  • Smaller when reliability is higher
SEE
  • Standard Error of Estimate
  • Formula: SD_Y * sqrt(1 - r_xy²)
  • Uses validity coefficient
  • Precision of a predicted score in regression
  • Applies when predicting criterion from predictor
  • Smaller when validity is higher
Sdiff
  • Standard Error of the Difference
  • Formula: sqrt(SEM1² + SEM2²)
  • Uses both scores' SEMs
  • Tests if discrepancy between two scores is significant
  • Also used in Reliable Change Index (RCI)
  • RCI > 1.96 = reliable change at .05 level

title: Tarasoff I vs. Tarasoff II: Duty to Warn vs. Protect
html:
Tarasoff I vs. Tarasoff II: Duty to Warn vs. Protect
Tarasoff I (1974) — Duty to Warn
  • Narrow obligation
  • Must directly warn the identifiable victim
  • Triggered by credible threat of violence
  • "Protective privilege ends where public peril begins"
Tarasoff II (1976) — Duty to Protect
  • Broader, current standard
  • Warn intended victim directly
  • Notify law enforcement
  • Hospitalize client (voluntary or involuntary)
  • Increase session frequency
  • Modify treatment plan
  • Supersedes Tarasoff I

title: Standard 6 Subsections at a Glance

Standard 6 Subsections at a Glance
6.01 Documentation

Maintain records in sufficient detail for continuity of care, research replication, billing accuracy, and legal compliance

6.02 Maintenance & Disposal

Protect confidentiality in storing, transferring, and disposing of records; plan for incapacity or death

6.03 Nonpayment

Cannot withhold records needed for emergency treatment due to nonpayment; may withhold in non-emergency per state law

6.04 Fee Arrangements

Establish fee agreements as early as feasible; include rates, payment schedule, cancellation policy, and nonpayment consequences

6.05 Bartering

Permissible only if not clinically contraindicated AND not exploitative

6.06 Billing Accuracy

No fraudulent claims — no upcoding, false diagnoses, or billing for services not rendered

6.07 Referral Fees

Fees must reflect services provided; paying or receiving kickbacks solely for referrals is prohibited

title: Stimulants vs. Atomoxetine: ADHD Treatment
html:
Stimulants vs. Atomoxetine: ADHD Treatment
Stimulants (Schedule II)
  • Methylphenidate, amphetamines
  • Block DA & NE reuptake (amphetamines also promote release)
  • First-line treatment for ADHD
  • Rapid onset of action
  • Abuse potential; controlled substance
  • Side effects: appetite loss, insomnia, elevated HR/BP
  • Rebound effects when wearing off
  • Growth suppression possible in children
Atomoxetine (Strattera)
  • Selective norepinephrine reuptake inhibitor (NRI)
  • Non-stimulant; NOT a controlled substance
  • No abuse potential
  • Takes 4–6 weeks for full effect
  • 24-hour continuous coverage
  • Preferred with comorbid SUD or anxiety
  • Black box warning: suicidal ideation in youth
  • Side effects: GI upset, dizziness, rare hepatotoxicity

Termination: When, How, and Why
Appropriate Termination (10.10a)

  • Client no longer needs service
  • Client is not likely to benefit
  • Continued service is causing harm
  • Therapist is threatened or endangered by client (10.10c)
Required Process (10.10b)
  • Provide pretermination counseling
  • Discuss progress and rationale
  • Suggest alternative service providers
  • Develop plan for maintaining gains
  • Exception: precluded by client or third-party payor actions
Abandonment (Always Prohibited)
  • Abrupt discontinuation without notice
  • No referrals provided
  • No transition planning
  • Applies even when client refuses to pay
